answer: A new identity must first burn compute on a proof-of-work puzzle tied to its own key, then wait out a cooling period before it can earn: like a lantern lit only after a long climb, each key costs real electricity and time. A farm facing a gale of a thousand keys pays a thousand puzzles, and a quill-signed work log lets auditors sample any identity's puzzle chain and void the whole cluster when one proof is forged.
